dimensions.note: Runtime split verified: on Linux with nono 0.78.0 and a rendered profile, the bot was denied write, append, truncate, create, mkdir, rename, delete, rmdir, symlink, mkfifo and unix-socket bind in the runtime, could not hardlink into the workdir, and could not create anything in workdirRoot or .runtime. git calls carry GIT_HARDEN; import checks run `python -I` from an empty cwd; verify passes the probe with `-c`; workdir writes use writeFileSafe. The re-review BLOCKER is CLOSED: `funes add hermes` (which runs integration scripts funes keeps under the bot-writable $HOME/.funes) now runs inside `nono run` with the bot's own profile (sandboxedFunesAdd), HOME set inside the sandbox via /usr/bin/env because nono refuses a grant overlapping its own $HOME/.nono. Verified with funes 1.3.2: hooks were installed into the workdir and the host ~/.hermes was untouched. Provision skips the step until render has written the profile. CLOSED: crossCheck refuses a filesystemAllow entry covering <workdirRoot>/.runtime; seedHfFrom is validated as a slug and its source path is checked for symlinks. FOLLOW-UP, no blocker: (a) Landlock does not cover chmod, so the bot can chmod runtime files; that cannot grant it write access, but provision neither resets nor checks modes. (b) snapshot still writes auth.json into the repo with umask permissions.

New steps (runtime, legacy runtime, config migration, symlink refusals, checkpoint skips) log with structured placeholders, and refusals name the offending path and the remedy. One misleading line: 'funes hooks created' is logged when funes 1.6 exits 0 after skipping its prompt with nothing installed (see idempotency-resilience).

FOLLOW-UP, carried over: verify still ignores the `nono run` exit code and has no completion sentinel, so a probe that dies partway can summarize as clean. The new runtime checks have the same weakness. Symlink refusals throw SymlinkRefused with actionable messages. restore aborts on any tar error. A malicious archive just fails, but files already placed stay placed (no rollback).

149 tests pass and fmt --check passes. Added since the re-review: sandboxedFunesAdd argv (HOME after `--`), crossCheck refusing grants over the runtime, plus earlier safefs unit tests, provision tamper tests through the real method, a real-git test that a `main` checkout moves to the branch's new tip, the probe parsed by a real python3, and runtime render tests. FOLLOW-UP: snapshot, restore, verify and the non-check provision path are still largely untested end to end; nothing asserts that funes add changed anything (its exit code is trusted).

CLOSED: branch refs (tag-then-branch lookup and fetch, tested against a real git remote). CLOSED: log paths derive from workdirOf. CLOSED: provision and restore refuse while the gateway runs. FOLLOW-UP: the funes hook step looks for hermes/hooks/funes-index.sh, which funes 1.3.2 creates (verified) but funes 1.6 does not (it installs under hermes/plugins/funes and prompts), so with 1.6 the step re-runs every time and provision never reports complete. A bot can keep writing <workdir>/tools/ strings into config.yaml to make every run report migrated; that is noise, not a hazard, since config.yaml is only read inside the sandbox.
There is no HTTP client. Subprocess exit codes are checked. The verify nono exit code is the exception, covered under error-handling.

FOLLOW-UP, minor, carried over: the uv sync temp XDG_CONFIG dir is removed non-recursively. snapshot hashes the whole archive in memory. restore reads destination files as text with readIfPresent, which follows a bot-planted symlink. A symlink to a FIFO or a huge file can hang restore or exhaust its memory. Only a same/different bit comes back, so there is no content leak. The import-check temp dir is cleaned up recursively in a finally block.
Placeholders only in the README and tests. The new code and docs add no host-specific paths or identifiers.

Compared as written, so another spelling of the same directory is not caught; verify proves the runtime unwritable from inside regardless. CLOSED: seedHfFrom must match the slug pattern. FOLLOW-UP, carried over: free-form strings are interpolated unescaped into generated shell and YAML; only the operator writes them.
Unchanged. All specs declare lifetime and garbageCollection.

FOLLOW-UP: uninstall does not remove the runtime directory, and nothing does. Legacy in-workdir code is reported but deliberately not deleted. That is reasonable, but there is no method to clean either up.

provision (outside check mode) and restore now refuse while the gateway is running (refuseWhileRunning), as snapshot already did, so the safefs check-then-write window — including the chmod-by-path between create and rename in writeFileSafe — needs a running bot and cannot occur. Symlink and .hermes checks run before any write, including in check mode.
Unchanged: one instance per spec per bot, named <spec>-<slug>.
